title: Cassandra: Efficient Enforcement of Sequential Execution for Cryptographic Programs
problem: Modern out-of-order processors violate constant-time programming assumptions by transiently executing unintended control-flow paths, enabling Spectre-class transient execution attacks against cryptographic code. Existing mitigations that address control-flow misspeculations impose high performance overhead by broadly restricting speculative execution.
motivation: Constant-time programming is the dominant practical defense for cryptographic side-channel attacks, but hardware speculation repeatedly undermines it, and no efficient hardware mechanism has closed this gap without major performance loss.
method: Cassandra disables branch prediction for constant-time cryptographic code regions and instead records and replays the deterministic sequential control flow using a Branch Trace Unit (BTU) added to the processor. Exploiting the observation that constant-time programs have mostly static control flow across runs and that cryptographic programs are loop-intensive with highly compressible control-flow patterns, Cassandra performs upfront branch analysis to compress control-flow traces stored in the BTU. The BTU then supplies fetch redirections from compressed trace storage, bypassing speculative branch prediction entirely for protected code regions.
key_novelty: Replacing the branch predictor with a record-and-replay mechanism using compressed control-flow traces for constant-time cryptographic code, achieving security without speculation overhead and even a net average speedup over an unsafe baseline.
contributions: Identification that constant-time program control flow is mostly static and highly compressible across different runs
Cassandra hardware/software mechanism: Branch Trace Unit (BTU) that stores compressed sequential control-flow traces and drives fetch redirections without speculative prediction
Upfront branch analysis pass that compresses loop-intensive cryptographic control-flow patterns for efficient trace storage
Demonstration of average 1.85% speedup over unsafe baseline processor while enforcing strong sequential execution security guarantees

metrics.speedup: average 1.85% speedup over unsafe baseline processor
metrics.other: strong security guarantee against Spectre-class transient execution attacks on constant-time code

baselines: unsafe baseline processor (with branch predictor, no Spectre mitigations)
limitations: Not discussed for cases where constant-time code control flow is not static or compressible across runs.
primary_theme: secure sequential execution enforcement for constant-time cryptographic code
